text:
jia: Quick sanity check — ran a small benchmark comparing multi-region p50/p95 for llama3-small int8 on h100 vs a100, with two routing modes: edge-proxy (default) and direct-pop. dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/latency/multi-region-hoplink (internal)
sam: nice, can you drop the numbers here? short table pls.
jia: sure — these are median of 3 runs, ~5k requests per run, mix of short/medium prompts (seq 64/256):

```
region  | route       | gpu  | p50(ms) | p95(ms)
US-EAST | direct-pop  | h100 | 34      | 120
US-EAST | edge-proxy  | h100 | 38      | 142
US-WEST | direct-pop  | h100 | 40      | 160
US-WEST | edge-proxy  | h100 | 48      | 210
EU-WEST | direct-pop  | a100 | 60      | 260
EU-WEST | edge-proxy  | a100 | 72      | 320
```

jia: TL;DR — edge-proxy adds small p50 overhead in same-region (5-15ms) but p95 tail blows up in cross-pop paths (US-WEST and EU-WEST) esp on a100 for longer seq. p95 variance correlates with extra hop count + proxy CPU saturation. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
sam: interesting that a100 eu p95 is so bad — did you try changing kernel selection or batching? any kernel mismatch logs?
jia: yes — kernel probe showed the runtime falling back to the generic attention kernel on some kv-cache sizes for a100 in eu-west. traces: `kernel=aten_generic` on slow tails. when forcing the optimized triton kernel for tt-attn we drop p95 by ~30ms in eu-west but p50 unchanged.
oliver: any difference if we change batch sizing or enable dynamic batching aggressively?
ja: dynamic batching helps throughput but increases tail on proxy path because of queuing at the proxy. For direct-pop, batching + small batch timeout = best p50->p95 ratio. For edge-proxy we need smaller batch windows or pre-warm connections.
maya: did you test quantization delta? int8 vs fp16 quality/regressions or perf tradeoffs?
ja: int8 (llm.int8-fast) gives ~10% p50 improvement on h100, but on a100 the quantized kernel falls back to slower path in eu-west for ~2% of requests causing p95 regressions. QA note: there's a small hallucination pattern change for long prompts — flagged in the eval suite. creating ticket.
lia: can we mitigate with routing policy — prefer local-pop direct and only use proxy for overflow? that seems like low-hanging.
oliver: agree. propose policy: prefer direct-pop for latency-sensitive routes (chat/generation) and leave proxy for embeddings/bulk tasks. we should also add a fail-open to direct-pop when proxy CPU > 70%.
jia: created a perf runbook snippet:
```
# quick load command
wrk -t8 -c200 -d120s --latency \ 
  -s scripts/llm_req.lua --  https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate?model=llama3-small-int8
```

jia: action items: oliver -> run 30m soak (5k rps) on US-WEST direct vs proxy, maya -> open eval ticket for int8/qregression, sam -> check runtime kernel mapping and kernel upgrade in eu-west, lia -> propose routing rule change in config repo. I'll attach the raw traces to the ticket. :memo:
